summary: Seychelles’ ecosystem pledges are primarily marine conservation commitments: it will protect at least 50% of its seagrass and mangrove ecosystems by 2025 and 100% by 2030, subject in places to external support, while implementing marine spatial planning and effectively managing 30% of its Exclusive Economic Zone as marine protected areas. The restoration agenda includes a recently commenced six-year project to restore 2.5 ha of coral reefs and build capacity, alongside NGO projects at multiple sites. Because the quantified commitments concern marine ecosystems, the supplied land-cover data—137 km² of forest (30.0%), 198 km² of agriculture (43.4%), and 6 km² of grassland (1.3%)—do not provide a direct denominator for measuring their scale.
